diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.
\|(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}(fg)\| \leq C(\alpha) \left( \|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \|(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}g\| + \|g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \|(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}f\| \right).

issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise inequality is false. Counterexample on Omega=[-pi,pi]^2 (constant in x_2): f=2+cos(k x_1), g=-f, both real and in every H^s. For alpha=1, (-Delta)^{1/2}(fg) = -(4k cos theta + k cos 2theta) while the right side is -2C k(2+cos theta)cos theta with C(1)=1; the claim reduces to 4c+2c^2-1 >= 4c+2c^2, i.e. -1>=0, failing at every point. Similarly at order 2, f=g=2+cos(k x_1) at x_1=pi/k gives LHS 6k^2>0 and RHS -2Ck^2<0. The proof is only a citation to a different setting and supplies no argument; only the norm-level consequence (standard Kato-Ponce) is true, while the stated pointwise bound (needed without absolute values for the pairing in Lemma conv_lemma, and applied there at order 1+alpha in [2,3]) is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the false pointwise inequality and replace it by the standard norm-level fractional Leibniz (Kato-Ponce) estimate; the a priori estimate in conv_lemma must then be re-derived by different means (see ISSUE-004).
issues.overall_effect: The stated pointwise tool is unreliable; the nonlinear energy estimate (est_nonl) in conv_lemma that invokes it loses its foundation, and with it the uniform bounds (bd1)-(bd3), the convergence/uniqueness conclusions of conv_lemma, thm:exisuq, and thm:spectral_accuracy (which uses bd3).
issues.title: False pointwise fractional Leibniz (product) inequality
issues.why_classification: A substantive stated lemma is false and must be withdrawn and replaced by a different (standard) inequality, which is more than a routine local fix; but a true substitute exists and no advertised final result is lost once the downstream argument is separately repaired.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}.
Then there exists a finite time $\bar T$ such that the following bounds hold

issues.failure_explanation: (bd3) holds only for t <= T-bar = 1/(C sqrt(D_0)) with D_0 = ||u_0||_{1+alpha}^2; it is not a uniform-in-time bound, so Remark remk_extnsn misreads (bd3) and its bootstrap is circular. Under the paper's own comparison bound the H^{1+alpha} norm at most doubles each step (D <= 4D_0), so the guaranteed step length shrinks geometrically (T-bar_k >= T-bar/2^k) and the iteration is only guaranteed to cover a finite time of order 2 T-bar. No global a priori H^{1+alpha} bound is established (the conserved Hamiltonian controls only H^{alpha/2}-type norms), so 'for all T >= 0' is unproven; for alpha<2 such global bounds are not available by the paper's methods.

issues.failure_explanation: Integrating eqn:fZK against a test function (using self-adjointness of (-Delta)^{alpha/2} and periodicity) gives (u_0,phi(0)) + int(u,phi_t) - int(u,(-Delta)^{alpha/2} phi_{x1}) + (1/2) int(u^2, phi_{x1}) = 0. The displayed (weaksoln) instead has +int(u,(-Delta)^{alpha/2} phi_{x1}) - (1/2) int(u^2, phi_{x1}); tracing it back, (weaksoln) is exactly the weak form of the x_1-reflected equation u_t + d_{x1}(-Delta)^{alpha/2}u - u d_{x1}u = 0, not of eqn:fZK. issues.title: Weak-solution formulation has reversed dispersive and nonlinear signs
issues.why_classification: A forced, local two-sign correction; with it the definition matches eqn:fZK and the limit argument goes through unchanged, with no loss of any claim, rate, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, employing the triangle inequality and the properties of the fractional Laplacian from Lemma \ref{lem:frac_properties} and Lemma \ref{lem:product_estimate}, and then utilizing the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality repeatedly alongside the Sobolev embedding results (Lemma \ref{lem:inverse_inequalities}), we have
(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}(fg)(\mathbf{x}) \leq C(\alpha) \left( f(\mathbf{x})(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}g(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x})(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}f(\mathbf{x}) \right)

issues.failure_explanation: In (est_nonl) the pointwise product estimate is substituted for (-Delta)^{(1+alpha)/2}(u_N d_{x1}u_N) inside an inner product against w = (-Delta)^{(1+alpha)/2}u_N, which changes sign. Even a valid pointwise bound A(x) <= B(x) cannot be paired against a sign-changing weight (one would need |A| <= |B|), and the needed pointwise bound at order 1+alpha in [2,3] is false anyway (ISSUE-001). Establishing (u_N d_{x1}u_N, (-Delta)^{1+alpha}u_N) <= C||u_N||_{1+alpha}^3 requires standard fractional commutator (Kato-Ponce/Coifman-Meyer) estimates for [(-Delta)^{(1+alpha)/2}, u_N]d_{x1}u_N, which are absent; the cited tools (triangle inequality, Cauchy-Schwarz, Sobolev/inverse inequalities) do not supply the step. Without (est_nonl), (diffine), (bd3), (bd2), and the convergence/uniqueness conclusions of conv_lemma are unproven.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid step by the standard energy argument: symmetrize (u d_{x1}u, (-Delta)^{1+alpha}u) via d_{x1}(u^2)/2 plus skew-adjointness, and bound the commutator [( -Delta)^{(1+alpha)/2}, u_N]d_{x1}u_N by Coifman-Meyer/Kato-Ponce estimates; for alpha in (1,2] this yields the claimed <= C||u_N||^3_{1+alpha} (alpha=1 is ISSUE-005).
issues.overall_effect: The uniform N-independent bounds (bd1)-(bd3), the compactness/convergence argument, uniqueness in conv_lemma, thm:exisuq, and thm:spectral_accuracy (which invokes bd3) all rest on this unproven estimate.
issues.title: Key a priori estimate inserts a pointwise inequality under a sign-changing pairing
issues.why_classification: The invalid step is repairable by a contained but nontrivial standard commutator-estimate argument, absent from the paper, that preserves the lemma's conclusions, rates, and scope for alpha in (1,2]; no new global architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The final step of (est_nonl) and the uniqueness argument require ||d_{x1}u_N||_{L^infty} <= C||u_N||_{1+alpha} (and ||d_{x1}(u-bar+w-bar)||_{L^infty} <= C(||u-bar||_{1+alpha}+||w-bar||_{1+alpha})), i.e. H^alpha(T^2) -> L^infty for d_{x1}u_N; in two dimensions this embedding holds only for alpha>1 and fails at alpha=1 (H^1 does not embed into L^infty). The alternative tool, the inverse inequality of Lemma inverse_inequalities, carries a factor N and destroys uniformity in N. Likewise thm:spectral_accuracy's proof needs ||d_{x1}u_N||_{L^infty} <= C from (bd3) and uses ||d_{x1}u||_{L^infty} <= C|u|_2 (the embedding H^2 -> W^{1,infty}, borderline-false in 2D). The advertised range alpha in [1,2], with alpha=1 (the Benjamin-Ono-related case highlighted in the introduction) included, is therefore not covered at the endpoint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict all statements to alpha in (1,2] (the numerical experiments themselves use alpha >= 1.2), or supply genuinely new endpoint estimates (e.g. L^p-based commutator estimates) for alpha=1; the source contains no such argument.
issues.overall_effect: All results proved through these embeddings (the a priori bound (bd3), uniqueness in conv_lemma, thm:exisuq, thm:spectral_accuracy) are unproven at alpha=1; the advertised regime [1,2] shrinks to (1,2] unless new endpoint arguments are supplied.
issues.title: Proofs fail at the advertised endpoint alpha = 1 (borderline Sobolev embedding in 2D)
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening (excluding the single endpoint alpha=1 of the advertised interval) leaves a recognizably comparable theory on (1,2]; the alternative repair requires nontrivial new estimates not present in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For brevity and to maintain focus on the novel aspects of our spectral discretization for the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK}, we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology.
where we assume that $r$ is proportional to $N$.
Let $r \geq 0$, $0 \leq l \leq \min\{r, \alpha+1\}$, $u \in C^1(\Omega)$,  $w \in H^r_{\text{per}}(\Omega)$, and $\widetilde{\Pi}_N$ be defined by \eqref{eq:proj_def}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proofs of thm:proj_error and lem:time_error are omitted; the cited source treats the one-dimensional Kawahara equation, and the adaptability of its duality argument to the 2D fractional operator is asserted, not demonstrated, even though these estimates are the paper's claimed novel error-analysis contribution. Moreover: (i) the sketched derivation of (proj_erro2) uses the false inequality |w|_r <= r! ||w|| (a seminorm with |k|^r weights cannot be bounded by r! times the L^2 norm; any w with a nonzero mode |k| > r/e violates it) plus an ad hoc 'assume r proportional to N'; the correct argument needs the analyticity bound |w|_r <= C r! sigma^{-r}, never established. (ii) The statements allow r >= 0, but the projection is defined (eq:proj_def, thm:added-1) only for r >= alpha+1, so the stated range is partly ill-posed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply complete proofs: an L^2 estimate from coercivity of K + u d_{x1} - (-Delta)^{alpha/2} d_{x1} (feasible for r >= alpha+1) and higher-order bounds via a duality/commutator argument adapted to the fractional operator; replace the exponential derivation by the standard analyticity bound |w|_r <= C r! sigma^{-r} optimized over r ~ N; restrict the stated range to r >= alpha+1.
issues.overall_effect: The projection error estimates (algebraic and exponential) underlying the optimal error analysis are unsupported; thm:spectral_accuracy, whose proof invokes (proj_erro), (time_error), (proj_erro2), inherits the gap.
issues.title: Modified-projection error estimates stated without valid proof; exponential derivation invalid
issues.why_classification: Missing but contained nontrivial arguments (duality for a nonlocal, nonsymmetric operator in 2D and a corrected analyticity argument); the statements are plausible and, once proven, preserve the advertised rates without architectural change.

issues.failure_explanation: For the key term ((u - Pi-tilde_N u) d_{x1}(Pi-tilde_N u), E_N): (i) the step ||d_{x1}u||_{L^infty} <= C|u|_2 uses H^2(T^2) -> W^{1,infty}, which is false in two dimensions (borderline; repairable from |u|_r only when r>2); (ii) even granting it, the product (N^{2-r}|u|_r)*||u - Pi-tilde_N u|| ~ N^{2-2r}, not N^{-2r}, so the displayed '<= CN^{-2r}' does not follow - the argument as written yields at best ||u - u_N|| = O(N^{1-r}). For the exponential part, (proj_erro2) is only an L^2 bound on u - Pi-tilde_N u and does not imply the displayed estimate, which needs derivative control of the projection error; moreover the hypothesis 'u_0 analytic' does not give the spatial analyticity of u(t) on [0,T] that applying (proj_erro2) to w = u(t) requires. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the broken estimation by the standard direct argument: test the difference of the exact equation and the scheme against E_N = u_N - Pi_N u in X_N, use skew-adjointness of (-Delta)^{alpha/2} d_{x1} on both the E_N and projection-error pieces (e.g. ((-Delta)^{alpha/2} d_{x1} eta, E_N) = -(eta, (-Delta)^{alpha/2} d_{x1} E_N) <= C||eta||), integrate u d_{x1} eta by parts, and apply Groenwall with E_N(0) = 0; this yields ||u - u_N|| <= CN^{-r} (and e^{-sigma N} under an analyticity assumption on u(t)) under the theorem's own hypotheses for alpha>1, t <= T-bar.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central rate guarantees (optimal algebraic order O(N^{-r}) and exponential convergence for analytic data) are unproven by the given argument; the fully discrete claim in Section 5 inherits this.
issues.title: Spectral-convergence proof: nonlinear term estimate invalid, optimal rate not established
issues.why_classification: The stated theorem is recoverable by a contained replacement argument using tools already in the paper, so no rate or scope is lost; but the fix is a nontrivial re-derivation of the proof, not a local edit.

\frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = e^{-L t} \mathcal{N}\left( e^{L t} V(t) \right) =: \mathcal{F}(t, V(t)).

Let $u$ be the exact solution of the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK} with initial data $u_0 \in H_{\mathrm{per}}^{r}(\Omega)$, $r \geq \alpha + 5$, and assume the nonlinear term $\mathcal{N}$ is sufficiently smooth.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is a formal Taylor expansion that never tracks N-dependence. The time derivatives of the transformed field F(t,V) = e^{-Lt} N(e^{Lt}V) contain powers of the diagonal operator L with norm ~ N^{1+alpha}: along the trajectory, V^{(5)} involves terms like L^4 N(U) and L^3 N_U(U)(LU). Bounding these uniformly in N requires roughly 4(1+alpha)+1 spatial derivatives of the (semi-discrete) solution, whereas the hypothesis r >= alpha+5 provides far less, and (bd3) gives only H^{1+alpha} control of u_N uniformly in N; moreover the hypothesis is posed on the PDE solution while T_{n+1} is defined along the semi-discrete trajectory. The uniform bound is simply asserted in the final sentence and is unestablished (and expected to fail) under the stated assumptions.
